testing|tests/unit/archive-budget.test.t.why_it_matters: Cancellation can regress to waiting for the next decompression output without this test failing: the assertion only checks the eventual cancellation error, which the existing cancelled() checks also produce. The new abort listener's purpose is to interrupt an outstanding reader.read(), and neither that interruption nor listener cleanup on success/error is asserted. A controlled stream that holds a read pending would distinguish prompt resource cancellation from eventual rejection after more output arrives.
evidence: src/formats/archive-budget.ts:308 --           const { value, done } = await reader.read();

Read-only instrumentation of the native stream confirmed the timer can abort during an active first-member read, but the current assertion observes only the final error and does not distinguish cancellation of that read from its ordinary completion followed by cancelled().

performance|src/formats/archive-budget.t.why_it_matters: A roughly 2.4 KiB ZIP with a 120 KiB worksheet containing repeated unterminated `<c ` prefixes makes preflight spend several seconds synchronously scanning XML; larger inputs within the resource budget grow quadratically. The tag regex retries its unbounded tail at every prefix, so expansion and cell limits do not prevent this CPU exhaustion and AbortSignal cannot interrupt the scan. Direct calls to the new preflight measured approximately 278 ms, 983 ms and 3742 ms for 10,000, 20,000 and 40,000 prefixes respectively.
evidence: Read-only Node 24 reproduction: preflight(workbook('', {extra: {'xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml': '<worksheet>' + '<c '.repeat(n)}})) took 277.8 ms at n=10000, 983.0 ms at n=20000, and 3741.5 ms at n=40000; largest archive was 2410 bytes with 122777 total expanded bytes.

reliability|src/formats/archive-budget.t.why_it_matters: A caller can receive successful preflight metrics even though its AbortSignal was aborted before preflight completed. The last member yields to the event loop after its final cancellation check, then returns without checking again; a caller awaiting this guard can therefore start parser work after cancellation. Checking the signal after that yield closes this explicit asynchronous cancellation window.
evidence: Read-only Node 24 reproduction using workbook('') and an AbortController aborted in the eighth/final setTimeout callback returned {"resolved":true,"aborted":true,"yields":8,"entries":8}.

adversarial|src/formats/archive-budget.t.why_it_matters: A valid worksheet containing literal text ref="ORDER-123" is rejected as an invalid worksheet address. The guard scans all XML text for apparent attributes, so customer cell contents become structural range declarations and prevent import. Restricting range inspection to real XML start-tag attributes preserves the structural limit without interpreting source values as metadata.
evidence: Constructed a workbook using the independent workbook() generator with A2 inline text <t>ref="ORDER-123"</t> and valid dimension A1:A2. Directly executing production preflight under Node 24 returned Invalid worksheet address, despite no invalid structural address.
The matched cell text is passed to rangeCells at lines 83-84, whose coordinate regex rejects ORDER-123 before any import can proceed.

adversarial|src/formats/archive-budget.t.why_it_matters: A number-format attribute longer than the mandatory 256-character cap passes the preflight when it contains an apostrophe inside double quotes. The regex ends the captured value at either quote character rather than its opening delimiter, so the unchanged archive can reach the future reader with an unbounded format that the guard claims to reject. Matching paired delimiters restores the established pre-parser limit.
evidence: Constructed a workbook with xl/styles.xml containing formatCode="0' followed by 300 zero characters and a closing double quote. Production preflight accepted it and returned eight verified entries with matching declared/actual expansion.

The regex captures only 0, and line 48 therefore measures one character instead of the complete 302-character value. docs/decisions/excel-fidelity.md requires format-code length to be bounded before parsing.
